description: Illustrative three-node slice of the KYE Cohesion Cascade graph, showing the two edge provenances a real graph carries: a hand-declared edge (the design-token → theme-CSS regeneration lockstep) and a machine-derived edge (a gate that literally reads a token file on disk, so the binding is evidence rather than assertion). The full graph is internal architecture and stays private; this example exists so the schema has a public conformance fixture.

publication_rule.rationale: The real cascade graph enumerates every canonical artefact and its derivation anchors — internal architecture. This illustrative slice is the public conformance fixture for the schema.

excluded_extensions.reason: §50 owns the page/content graph; page↔page links are content relationships, not producer/consumer dataflow.

always_node_paths.reason: Every executable script is a component and must be a node whether or not another node names it — otherwise a generator stays invisible and its output cannot be known to be generated.

nodes.summary: Light-theme CSS custom properties generated from the canonical color tokens. Hand-edits are rejected and routed back to the token file.
CI gate color-canonical (hand-authored enforcer). Reads the canonical token file and verifies the generated theme CSS matches it.
Derived node — generated artefact written by scripts/build-example.mjs. Edit the source, never this file.

edges.summary: A change to the canonical color tokens MUST regenerate the light-theme CSS in the same commit.
